# Freeze repeated compiler preparation benchmark and lifecycle validation

GitHub: https://github.com/misofm/engine/issues/875

## Outcome and dependencies

Depends on [#872](https://github.com/misofm/engine/issues/872), [#873](https://github.com/misofm/engine/issues/873) and [#874](https://github.com/misofm/engine/issues/874). Deliver an executable, preflighted comparison in the existing benchmark tool, without running its official timed workloads.

## Exact implementation slice

Own `tools/bench/src/compiler_scratch.rs`, its dispatcher/manifest entries, a small fixture module if needed, and `scripts/run-compiler-scratch-benchmark.sh` plus `scripts/check-compiler-scratch-records.py`. Construct the experimental workspace through graph-compiler test support and pass it through the accepted ordinary host workspace entry; no second host preparation pipeline or pool-specific host API. Do not create a second benchmark framework. Reuse bench-support metadata, hashing, counters and statistics.

Freeze all fixtures, operations, policy order, repetitions, row schema, timing/count boundaries, retention cap and output paths in a checked configuration before capture. Use 48 kHz/q128, native pinned AVX2/FMA, the shipped release profile, the same source/toolchain for all four policies, and a fixed 1 MiB post-call scratch-retention cap (an experimental setting, not a product default). Test zero-cap behavior separately.

Two workload families suffice: (1) the existing graph-only 256-track/1024-route/32-submix fixture, preserving its conformance factory and effect preparation outside the graph-compile interval; (2) real native host preparation from the existing nine-track EQ and 64-track intended-console fixtures, which use supported native effects. Do not send `conformance.delay` through the host's native registry. No new large fixture corpus or 65,537-track timed stress row.

Freeze lifecycle sequences: cold preparation with fresh workspace; eight same-size replacements; `small -> large -> small` repeated twice; and `valid -> late-rejected candidate -> valid` repeated twice. Keep the active complete host alive during replacement preparation. For valid replacements hold old and candidate simultaneously, then advance the benchmark-owned active host between blocks and drop the displaced host on the control thread. This measures the two-host memory overlap; it does not certify protocol admission or retirement-queue behavior. Include session inputs, active/candidate hosts, queues and retained scratch in lifetime/byte observation, rather than summing estimates. Do not preconstruct eight effect/session copies and accidentally call their memory a one-candidate peak.

Graph-only records report graph compilation; native-host records report full preparation from an already compiled session. Parsing, fixture generation, hashing/formatting and rendering are outside these intervals. Any workspace reset or post-call retention cleanup needed to produce a ready candidate is inside. Record phase boundaries and bytes before preparation, at candidate readiness, after retirement and after workspace release. No percentile claims based on two rounds; preserve individual observations and descriptive summaries.

Build separate direct-System timing and audited byte-instrumented executables from the same source, toolchain and release profile, differing only in their declared measurement features. Verify and record the effective allocator mode; default bench-support counters must not remain active in timing records. The direct-System executable does no render calls; rendering, PCM and allocator/free audits run in the audited correctness executable. Its dispatcher refuses other benchmark subjects under the special timing mode. Count allocations and pool backing/occupancy in the memory pass. Each policy/workload uses fresh processes for RSS attribution; label OS high-water values as covering process setup and warmup too, not as exact per-stage RSS. A single supervisor invocation runs one whole-sequence warmup and exactly two measured rounds per declared row/pass. Fixed ordering is recorded; no tuning, adaptive repetition or retry after results.

## Frozen policy order and initial state

Use schema IDs in this order: `std_fresh`, `std_reused`, `api2_global_fresh`, `api2_bump_reused`. Fresh policies create and release the selected array owners for every preparation. Reused policies retain their vector capacities or arena backing under the same retention cap. Both collection controls and both practical candidates use the same algorithm slices.

Cold means empty workspace capacity at every measured preparation, not cold OS/code caches. Its warmup owner is disposable. For steady reuse, initialize one active fixture and warm the retained workspace with one whole eight-replacement sequence, then continue with that same workspace for two measured eight-replacement rounds. Reclaim each displaced host before the next replacement so live-state counts stay fixed. For shape changes and rejection, use a disposable warmup sequence; each measured round starts from a new workspace and the identical initial small/valid active host, prepared outside the interval using separate ephemeral scratch. Capacity growth during the prescribed sequence is measured. Do not carry a large previous round's capacity into the next round. The graph-only family uses the analogous retained graph artifact ownership. Record these state rules in each row; compare equal modes/phases, not differently primed starts.

The 1 MiB cap limits requested scratch backing retained after a call, including pool chunk metadata/padding visible in backing requests. Global allocator metadata is excluded consistently. Report pool occupancy separately and do not sum it into physical backing bytes. Before official capture, untimed correctness/shape validation must verify the chosen successful large fixture fits this cap for each policy; this validation is distinct from the zero-workload runner preflight. If it does not fit, amend/freeze the workload contract before timing rather than tuning after measurements.

## Zero-workload preflight and acceptance

Before capture, test argument parsing, schema validation, duplicate/missing/extra rows, malformed numbers, output create-new/overwrite refusal, raw stdout/stderr persistence, and propagation of child nonzero/signal/shell pipeline failures using synthetic child data. Preflight must launch zero official workload invocations. Untimed correctness tests use small fixtures and verify semantic/hash/PCM equality, error ownership, retention cleanup, and actual zero-allocation/free rendering after workspace release. The pool/global control separates collection implementation differences from allocation policy; std retained versus pool is the practical adoption comparison.

Source/validator checkpoint and root review must pass before [#876](https://github.com/misofm/engine/issues/876). If harness scope expands beyond this boundary, split before implementation.

## Delegation and checkpoint contract

Assign one fresh `gpt-6-luna` agent with `reasoning_effort=max` to this bounded issue. Root briefs/reviews the issue and owns exact-path commits, integration and GitHub synchronization. This user-selected model workflow supersedes historical Terra defaults for this series. Each attempt is one coherent implementation pass plus one root adversarial verdict; maximum five attempts, then preserve evidence and split/rebrief. Root commits every compiling, focused-green tranche before any further implementation layers on it. No implementation slice should exceed half a working day; split before expanding beyond the named boundary. Independent tooling may run in its own worktree/target; overlapping source owners are sequential. Final independent verification remains the user's fresh Astra XHIGH review after implementation and capture. Status: scoped; implementation and official measurements have not started.
